summary: Texas Forest Service lookout on a hill near Scottsville, Harrison County; one of 74 TFS towers in 1943 and listed as gone; no build date or site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Texas list; no source describes what remains at the site

events.note: Described in a 14 Nov 1943 newspaper item (quoted on Central US Lookouts) as one of the Texas Forest Service's 74 lookout towers and one of three in Harrison County
Patrolman Carl J. McBrayer spotted fires from the tower

evidence.supports: tower stood on a hilltop near Scottsville
evidence.quote: the nearly bald summit of a hill near Scottsville

evidence.supports: one of the Texas Forest Service's 74 lookout towers in 1943
evidence.quote: one of the Texas Forest Service's 74 lookout towers

evidence.supports: one of three towers in Harrison County
evidence.quote: The Scottsville tower is one of three located in Harrison county.

evidence.supports: Patrolman Carl J. McBrayer spotted fires from the tower in 1943
evidence.quote: From this tower Patrolman Carl J. McBrayer is able to spot fires in the far reaches of the area.

evidence.supports: the tower was dedicated to guard acres of timberland
evidence.quote: acres of timberland it is dedicated to guard

evidence.supports: the Texas list records the tower as gone

sources.title: Scottsville #52 (Texas Lookouts, quoting The Marshall News Messenger, 14 Nov 1943)

notes_for_editor: Only one substantive source: a 1943 newspaper item quoted on a lookout-history site. The original Marshall News Messenger article was not read; checking it on the Portal to Texas History could add a build date or height. No build date, height, design or fate date found. Access and current condition unknown. The FFLA list gives no register number.
